newsitem.title: USA: Dry days aid Minnesota harvest, deplete moisture.
newsitem.headline: Dry days aid Minnesota harvest, deplete moisture.

text.p: Sunny, warm days allowed good harvest progress in the week ended Sunday but dry weather further depleted soil moisture, Minnesota's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly update.
Spring wheat was 55 percent harvested, compared with the five-year average of 60 percent.
But soil moisture decreased to 53 percent adequate to surplus, down five percent from the previous week.
"The warm weather was needed to advance row crop development which lags normal development by 10 to 14 days," the report said.
"Moisture is also needed for corn ears and bean pods to fully develop."

Corn was rated two percent very poor, 10 percent poor, 33 percent fair, 46 percent good and nine percent excellent. Corn in the dough stage improved to 47 percent of the crop, compared with average of 72 percent.
Soybeans were rated one percent very poor, eight percent poor, 35 fair, 50 percent good and six percent excellent.
Pasture condition was rated nine percent very poor, 23 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 28 percent good and two percent excellent.
